newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: UK's Clarke backs political control over EMU pact.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke backs political control over EMU pact.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said he backed French demands for a political say in enforcing fiscal discipline after monetary union.
"France had a good point which we supported them on," Clarke said of the compromise proposal worked out in a marathon finance ministers' session which ended early on Friday morning.

Germany has been pressing for a stability pact with rigid rules on fining countries which run fiscal deficits of more than three percent of GDP after economic and monetary union (EMU), set to start on January 1, 1999.
France and others have argued that there has to be some political leeway in imposing fines to avoid driving a country with genuine fiscal problems deeper into the red.
EU leaders were due to discuss the compromise text at a two-day summit which they opened in Dublin on Friday.
Clarke said, "The whole thing has to remain under the political control of the ministers of the nation states who are taking part (in EMU)."

The compromise was not a fudge, he said. "It's just to ensure that finance ministers and elected governments of the nation states maintain their political control over the whole process, and still you combine that with a sensible stability pact."
